newsitem.title: USA: Colgate-Palmolive quarter aided by new product sales.
newsitem.headline: Colgate-Palmolive quarter aided by new product sales.

text.p: Personal care products giant Colgate-Palmolive Co. Thursday reported higher second-quarter earnings, fuelled by strong new product sales and increases in global advertising.
The maker of Colgate, Palmolive, Mennen, and Ajax products, as well as Hill's pet foods, said worldwide unit volume grew 9 percent in the second quarter.

"Market shares increased in most areas, with new products receiving excellent consumer response. Ongoing cost savings and restructuring drove gross profit margin up 180 basis points, allowing for a worldwide increase in business-building advertising of almost 20 percent, at the same time that earnings grew sharply," Chairman Reuben Mark said.
Colgate said earnings rose to $175.8 million, or 58 cents a share, from $148.9 million, or 49 cents a share, a year earlier.
Sales rose to $2.3 billion from $2.17 billion in the year-earlier period. Sales would have increased 9 percent had it not been for the effects of foreign currency translations, the company said.

Colgate said it had volume growth in every division. Colgate-Latin America and Hill's Pet Nutrition had volume growth of 12 percent each, Colgate-Europe rose 8 percent, Colgate-North America rose 7 percent and Colgate-Asia/Africa rose 5 percent.
Currently, Colgate-Latin America comprises 25 percent of company sales and Colgate-Europe 23 percent.

Colgate-North America, which contributes 22 percent of sales, said results were driven by sales of the new Colgate Whitening with Baking Soda & Peroxide toothpaste, the premium Colgate Wave toothbrush, Palmolive Pots & Pans dishwashing detergent, Softsoap body wash and other new products.
Colgate-Palmolive stock was up 62.5 cents at $76 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
